text:
That

afternoon, in the promenade, mad

with love, my sweet idolized one

offered me

the eglantine of her mouth.


And the basalt Buddha smiled...

Another came afterward, and his

charms

stole her from me; I made an appointment with her, and in the shade

we exchanged epistles

and curls.


And the basalt Buddha smiled...

Today it is a year since the love

lost.

I return to the place and, since I am exhausted

after long walking,

I climb to the top

of the pedestal on which the symbol rests.


Defeated and bloody the day dies,

and in the arms of the basalt

Buddha

the mysterious moon surprises me.

translation.title: I Loved the Blue with Ardor
translation.editorial_note: The catalog title differs from the embedded Buddha poem, so the body follows the source line breaks.
